primary_claim: SAEBench, a suite of 8 diverse SAE evaluations run across 200+ trained sparse autoencoders on Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B, shows that SAE quality results are nuanced with no single ideal SAE configuration — the best SAE depends on the specifics of the downstream task, so results cannot be collapsed into one number.
contradicts_or_qualifies: Most prior SAE improvement work merely measures whether reconstruction improves at a given sparsity, which can miss problems like uninterpretable high-frequency latents or increased feature composition
limitations_stated: This is a beta version of SAEBench
Results cannot be combined into a single number without obscuring tradeoffs between SAE configurations
quote: We find that these evaluation results are nuanced and there is no one ideal SAE configuration - instead, the best SAE varies depending on the specifics of the downstream task.
